payload.goal:
Add exactly 4 independent warehouse analytics modules to the verified W1 codebase.
Create src/analytics/contracts.ts exporting WarehouseProjection with a readonly id and project(scenario), where project returns the answer to that module's question.
Each module answers one question, computed from the W1 Scenario, layout and inventory exports:
- src/analytics/projection-01.ts exports the projection "zone-unit-totals": Total units stored in each zone, keyed by zone id. Its focused tests live in src/analytics/projection-01.test.ts.
- src/analytics/projection-02.ts exports the projection "sku-unit-totals": Total units of each SKU across the whole warehouse, keyed by SKU id. Its focused tests live in src/analytics/projection-02.test.ts.
- src/analytics/projection-03.ts exports the projection "bin-occupancy": How many bins hold stock, how many are empty, and how many exist. Its focused tests live in src/analytics/projection-03.test.ts.
- src/analytics/projection-04.ts exports the projection "sku-bin-spread": Number of distinct bins each SKU occupies, keyed by SKU id. Its focused tests live in src/analytics/projection-04.test.ts.
A module must not import another module; it may import only the fixed contract and W1 exports.
Every answer must be derived from the scenario at run time. Do not hardcode results, and do not duplicate the W1 inventory or layout calculations.
Create src/analytics/registry.ts as the sole consumer of every module, returning all projections in the order the modules are listed above, with its own tests in src/analytics/registry.test.ts.
Preserve all existing W1 behaviour and checks.
Add a package script named study:wide-graph that writes exactly one JSON object to stdout and no other output.
Its JSON must be { "schemaVersion": 1, "moduleCount": 4, "scenario": "thesis-seed-2026", "projections": [ { "projectionId": "<the module's projection id>", "value": <that module's answer> }, … ] } with exactly 4 entries in the order the modules are listed above.
Two invocations from the same commit must emit byte-identical JSON.

root.title: Warehouse analytics modules
root.objective: Add four runtime-derived warehouse analytics projections, a registry, focused tests, and a deterministic study:wide-graph package script without changing existing W1 behavior.
expectedOutcomes: A shared WarehouseProjection contract exists under src/analytics.
Exactly four analytics modules compute their answers from W1 scenario, layout, and inventory exports at run time.
Each projection has focused tests and does not import another projection module.
The registry is the sole internal consumer of every projection module and returns them in the required order.
The study:wide-graph script emits byte-identical single-object JSON for the thesis seed scenario.
Existing W1 checks remain covered.

complexitySignals.rationale: The work is broad across new analytics files, test discovery, and package scripts, but uses existing W1 domain exports without changing their contracts.

cut.rationale: Each projection is an independently testable runtime calculation. The contract, registry, and command are separate because they define integration points and deterministic output acceptance.

children.title: Analytics projection contract
children.objective: Create the shared WarehouseProjection contract used by every analytics module and the registry.
expectedOutcomes: src/analytics/contracts.ts exports WarehouseProjection.
WarehouseProjection exposes readonly id and project(scenario).
The scenario parameter is compatible with the existing W1 scenario shape.

complexitySignals.rationale: Small new exported type, but it becomes the shared contract for every projection and registry consumer.

children.title: Zone unit totals projection
children.objective: Implement and test the zone-unit-totals projection from W1 scenario inventory and layout data.
expectedOutcomes: src/analytics/projection-01.ts exports a WarehouseProjection with id zone-unit-totals.
project(scenario) returns total units stored in each zone keyed by zone id.
The result is computed from W1 exports at run time without hardcoded answers or duplicated inventory/layout calculations.
src/analytics/projection-01.test.ts verifies the projection against the thesis seed scenario and relevant edge expectations.

complexitySignals.rationale: Requires understanding how inventory is assigned to layout zones, but remains isolated to one projection and its tests.

children.title: SKU unit totals projection
children.objective: Implement and test the sku-unit-totals projection from W1 scenario inventory data.
expectedOutcomes: src/analytics/projection-02.ts exports a WarehouseProjection with id sku-unit-totals.
project(scenario) returns total units of each SKU across the whole warehouse keyed by SKU id.
The result is computed from W1 exports at run time without hardcoded answers or duplicated inventory calculations.
src/analytics/projection-02.test.ts verifies the projection against the thesis seed scenario and relevant aggregation behavior.

complexitySignals.rationale: Narrow inventory-only aggregation with one exported projection and focused tests.

children.title: Bin occupancy projection
children.objective: Implement and test the bin-occupancy projection from W1 scenario inventory and layout data.
expectedOutcomes: src/analytics/projection-03.ts exports a WarehouseProjection with id bin-occupancy.
project(scenario) returns how many bins hold stock, how many are empty, and how many exist.
The result is computed from W1 exports at run time without hardcoded answers or duplicated inventory/layout calculations.
src/analytics/projection-03.test.ts verifies occupied, empty, and total bin counts.

complexitySignals.rationale: Combines layout bin existence with inventory stock presence and needs tests for all three reported values.

children.title: SKU bin spread projection
children.objective: Implement and test the sku-bin-spread projection from W1 scenario inventory data.
expectedOutcomes: src/analytics/projection-04.ts exports a WarehouseProjection with id sku-bin-spread.
project(scenario) returns the number of distinct bins each SKU occupies keyed by SKU id.
The result is computed from W1 exports at run time without hardcoded answers or duplicated inventory calculations.
src/analytics/projection-04.test.ts verifies distinct-bin counting, including multiple stock entries for the same SKU.

complexitySignals.rationale: Narrow projection, with validation focused on distinctness rather than summing units.

children.title: Analytics registry
children.objective: Create and test the sole registry consumer that returns all four projections in the required order.
expectedOutcomes: src/analytics/registry.ts imports all four projection modules and returns them in the required order.
No analytics projection imports another projection module.
src/analytics/registry.test.ts verifies projection ids, count, order, and that registry entries can project the thesis seed scenario.

complexitySignals.rationale: The registry is a small integration point but owns ordering and the sole-consumer constraint for modules.

children.title: Deterministic wide graph study script
children.objective: Add the study:wide-graph package script and implementation that emits exactly one deterministic JSON object for the thesis seed scenario.
expectedOutcomes: package.json defines study:wide-graph.
The script emits exactly one JSON object to stdout and no other output.
The JSON has schemaVersion 1, moduleCount 4, scenario thesis-seed-2026, and four projection entries in registry order.
Two invocations from the same commit are byte-identical.
The test script or focused test coverage includes analytics tests while preserving existing W1 tests.

complexitySignals.rationale: Touches package command configuration and must verify exact stdout shape, determinism, and continued W1 test coverage.
